15300-mike-flannery-on-duty-and-off.title: On Duty and Off
15300-mike-flannery-on-duty-and-off.creator: Ellis Parker Butler
15300-mike-flannery-on-duty-and-off.description: A book by Ellis Parker Butler. Flannery stuck out his under jaw, and his eyes blazed. For nothing at all he would have let Timmy have a fist in the side of the head, but what was the use? There are some folks you can't pound sense into, and Timmy was one of them.

65121-hindu-magic-an-expose-of-the-trick.title: Yogis And Fakirs Of India
65121-hindu-magic-an-expose-of-the-trick.creator: Unknown
65121-hindu-magic-an-expose-of-the-trick.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. As the trick is usually exhibited, it is somewhat as follows: The native comes forward, almost nude, being covered only with a small loin cloth, of such small compass that the onlooker can see clearly that there is nothing hidden in or about it or the performer.

arxiv-1906-02979.title: A Wind of Change: Detecting and Evaluating Lexical Semantic Change across Times and Domains
arxiv-1906-02979.creator: Dominik Schlechtweg, Anna Hätty, Marco del Tredici, Sabine Schulte im Walde
arxiv-1906-02979.description: Abstract We perform an interdisciplinary large-scale evaluation for detecting lexical semantic divergences in a diachronic and in a synchronic task: semantic sense changes across time, and semantic sense changes across domains. Our work addresses the superficialness and lack of comparison in assessing models of diachronic lexical change, by bringing together and extending benchmark models on a common state-of-the-art evaluation task.

arxiv-2209-13608.title: Revisiting the Logarithmic Corrections to the Black Hole Entropy
arxiv-2209-13608.description: Abstract Logarithmic corrections to the entropy of extremal black holes have been successfully used to accurately match degeneracies from microscopic constructions to calculations of the gravitational path integral. In this paper, we revisit the problem of deriving such corrections for the case of extremal black holes, either non-supersymmetric or supersymmetric, and for near-extremal black holes.

arxiv-2404-03776.title: Four-of-a-kind? Comprehensive atmospheric characterisation of the HR 8799 planets with VLTI/GRAVITY
arxiv-2404-03776.creator: E. Nasedkin ,, P. Mollière, S. Lacour, M. Nowak, L. Kreidberg, T. Stolker, J. J. Wang, W. O. Balmer, J. Kammerer, J. Shangguan, R. Abuter, A. Amorim, R. Asensio-Torres, M. Benisty, J.-P. Berger, H. Beust, S. Blunt, A. Boccaletti, M. Bonnefoy, H. Bonnet, M. S. Bordoni, G. Bourdarot, W. Brandner, F. C
arxiv-2404-03776.description: Abstract With four companions at separations from 16 to 71 au, HR 8799 is a unique target for direct imaging, presenting an opportunity for a comparative study of exoplanets with a shared formation history. Combining new VLTI/GRAVITY observations obtained within the ExoGRAVITY program with archival data, we performed a systematic atmospheric characterisation across all four planets.

arxiv-2405-02200.title: Position: Why We Must Rethink Empirical Research in Machine Learning
arxiv-2405-02200.creator: Moritz Herrmann, F. Julian D. Lange, Katharina Eggensperger, Giuseppe Casalicchio, Marcel Wever, Matthias Feurer, David Rügamer, Eyke Hüllermeier, Anne-Laure Boulesteix, Bernd Bischl
arxiv-2405-02200.description: Abstract We warn against a common but incomplete understanding of empirical research in machine learning that leads to non-replicable results, makes findings unreliable, and threatens to undermine progress in the field. To overcome this alarming situation, we call for more awareness of the plurality of ways of gaining knowledge experimentally but also of some epistemic limitations.

arxiv-2408-13885.title: Neural Spacetimes for DAG Representation Learning
arxiv-2408-13885.creator: Haitz Sáez de Ocáriz Borde, Anastasis Kratsios, Marc T. Law, Xiaowen Dong, Michael Bronstein
arxiv-2408-13885.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Haitz Sáez de Ocáriz Borde, Anastasis Kratsios, Marc T. Law, Xiaowen Dong, Michael Bronstein. We propose a class of trainable deep learning-based geometries called Neural SpaceTimes (NSTs), which can universally represent nodes in weighted Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) as events in a spacetime manifold.

arxiv-2411-15364.title: Exploring Facets of Language Generation in the Limit
arxiv-2411-15364.creator: Moses Charikar, Chirag Pabbaraju
arxiv-2411-15364.description: Abstract The recent work of Kleinberg and Mullainathan (2024) provides a concrete model for language generation in the limit: given a sequence of examples from an unknown target language, the goal is to generate new examples from the target language such that no incorrect examples are generated beyond some point.

arxiv-2501-14556.title: A sandbox study proposal for private and distributed health data analysis
arxiv-2501-14556.creator: Rickard Brannvall, Hanna Svensson, Kannaki Kaliyaperumal, Håkan Burden, Susanne Stenberg
arxiv-2501-14556.description: Abstract This paper presents a sandbox study proposal focused on the distributed processing of personal health data within the Vinnova-funded SARDIN project. The project aims to develop the Health Data Bank (Hälsodatabanken in Swedish), a secure platform for research and innovation that complies with the European Health Data Space (EHDS) legislation.

arxiv-2505-20021.title: Decomposing Complex Visual Comprehension into Atomic Visual Skills for Vision Language Models
arxiv-2505-20021.creator: Hyunsik Chae †, Seungwoo Yoon †, Jaden Park ⋆, Chloe Yewon Chun †
arxiv-2505-20021.description: Abstract Recent Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated impressive multimodal comprehension and reasoning capabilities, yet they often struggle with trivially simple visual tasks. In this work, we focus on the domain of basic 2D Euclidean geometry and systematically categorize the fundamental, indivisible visual perception skills, which we refer to as atomic visual skills.

arxiv-2506-03164.title: Test-Time Scaling of Diffusion Models via Noise Trajectory Search
arxiv-2506-03164.creator: Vignav Ramesh, Morteza Mardani
arxiv-2506-03164.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Vignav Ramesh, Morteza Mardani. The iterative and stochastic nature of diffusion models enables test-time scaling , whereby spending additional compute during denoising generates higher-fidelity samples. Increasing the number of denoising steps is the primary scaling axis, but this yields quickly diminishing returns. Instead optimizing the noise trajectory —the sequence of injected noise vectors—is promising, as the specific noise realizations critically affect sample quality; but this is challenging due to a high-dimensional search space, complex noise-outcome interactions, and costly trajectory evaluations.

arxiv-2510-23398.title: Free-space quantum interface of a single atomic tweezer array with light
arxiv-2510-23398.creator: Yakov Solomons ∗, Roni Ben-Maimon ∗, Arpit Behera ∗, Ofer Firstenberg, Nir Davidson, Ephraim Shahmoon
arxiv-2510-23398.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yakov Solomons ∗, Roni Ben-Maimon ∗, Arpit Behera ∗, Ofer Firstenberg, Nir Davidson, Ephraim Shahmoon. We present a practical approach for interfacing light with a two-dimensional atomic tweezer array. Typical paraxial fields are poorly matched to the array’s multi-diffraction-order radiation pattern, thus severely limiting the interface coupling efficiency. Instead, we propose to design a field mode that naturally couples to the array: it consists of a unique superposition of multiple beams corresponding to the array’s diffraction orders.

pmc-10615441.creator: Dinesh Nathwani, Michael McNicholas, Alister Hart, Jonathan Miles, Vladimir Bobić
pmc-10615441.description: :We previously conducted a single-arm, prospective study in which 31 patients (mean age [and standard deviation], 42.5 ± 11.3 years) with cartilage lesions were treated with use of the BioPoly Partial Resurfacing Knee Implant. Treatment outcomes were compared with those reported for the standard of care, microfracture.

pmc-11311667.title: Predictors of Meat Reduction: The Case of Slovenia
pmc-11311667.creator: Andrej Kirbiš, Vanesa Korže, Maruša Lubej
pmc-11311667.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Health, environmental, and animal advocacy organisations emphasise reducing or eliminating high meat consumption due to its adverse effects on health, sustainability, climate change, and animal welfare. Increasingly, people are deciding to reduce their meat consumption frequency. Our study aimed to examine predictors of meat reduction among Slovenian consumers, focusing on gender, age, partner and children status, size of residential settlement, socioeconomic status, and political orientation. We conducted a survey using non-probability sampling.

pmc-11431417.title: Increased Distress in Neurooncological Patients, a Monocentric Longitudinal Study: When to Screen Which Patient?
pmc-11431417.creator: Franziska Staub-Bartelt, Julia Steinmann, Maren Wienand, Michael Sabel, Marion Rapp, Haruhiro Higashida
pmc-11431417.description: Objective: Neurooncological patients are well-known to experience an increased psycho-oncological burden with a negative impact on distress, therapy adherence, quality of life, and finally survival. But still, psycho-oncological screening and support is rare, with ongoing discussion about specific screening time points and impact factors. Therefore, we analysed the psycho-oncologic treatment demand at specific disease-related time points throughout therapy.

pmc-11512523.title: Review of Excessive Cytosolic DNA and Its Role in AIM2 and cGAS-STING Mediated Psoriasis Development
pmc-11512523.creator: Tongtong Xu, Xiaojing Zhong, Nana Luo, Wenyi Ma, Pingsheng Hao
pmc-11512523.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). In psoriasis, keratinocytes are triggered by factors, such as infection or tissue damage, to release DNA, which thereby activates plasmacytoid dendritic cells and macrophages to induce inflammation, thickened epidermis, and parakeratosis. The recognition of double‐stranded (ds)DNA facilitates the activation of cytoplasmic DNA sensors absent in melanoma 2 (AIM2) inflammasome assembly and cyclic guanosine monophosphate adenosine monophosphate (cGAMP) synthase (cGAS) - stimulator of interferon gene (STING) pathway, both of which play a pivotal role in mediating the inflammatory response and driving the progression

pmc-12404560.title: Digital soil mapping in support of voluntary carbon market programs in agricultural land
pmc-12404560.creator: James R. Kellner, Christian Clanton, Kirk M. Demuth, Mitchell Donovan, Y. Katherina Feng, Mage Khim-Young, Julia Maddalena, Rose Rustowicz, David Schurman
pmc-12404560.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Voluntary carbon market (VCM) programs in agriculture depend on accurate measurements of soil organic carbon (SOC) that can be deployed at scale efficiently, but barriers are preventing widespread adoption. To overcome these challenges, we developed a digital soil mapping (DSM) framework driven by machine-learning and numerous spatial covariates, including long-term climate proxies, short-term climate and weather-related variables, topographic and edaphic measurements, and remote sensing time-series summaries.

pmc-12597602.title: The Uncommon ECG Signature of Hypokalemia: Left Main Coronary Equivalent
pmc-12597602.creator: Mahsa Borjzadehgashtaseb, Alireza Arzhangzadeh, Roozbeh Narimani Javid, Hamed Bazrafshan Drissi, Salma Nozhat, Sasan Shafiei, Davar Aledavood, Soorena Khorshidi
pmc-12597602.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This case highlights that severe hypokalemia can mimic the ECG findings associated with left main coronary artery disease. Early recognition and appropriate correction of electrolyte disturbances are essential in managing such presentations and avoiding misdiagnosis and unnecessary invasive procedures.Keywords: electrocardiogram, hypokalemia, ischemic heart disease, left main coronary equivalent

Introduction

Hypokalemia is a frequently encountered electrolyte imbalance in clinical practice, often leading to a variety of electrocardiographic (ECG) changes.

pmc-12655634.title: Epidemiologic Characteristics of 1.4 Million Multiplex PCR Tests for 12 Urogenital and Sexually Transmitted Infection Pathogens in Korea (2021–2024)
pmc-12655634.creator: Soyoun Shin
pmc-12655634.description: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) remain a global health concern, but large-scale multiplex PCR surveillance data are limited. This study aimed to characterize sex- and age-specific distributions, temporal patterns, and co-infection dynamics of 12 urogenital and sexually transmitted infection (STI) pathogens in Korea. We retrospectively analyzed 1,399,431 multiplex PCR test records (902,713 females, 496,718 males) collected nationwide between 2021 and 2024.

pmc-12689631.title: Search-and-remove genome editing allows selection of cells by DNA sequence
pmc-12689631.creator: Luise Fast, Madina Omar, Philipp Kanis, Theresa Schaffer, Deepika Chowdhury, Eva Rakava, Svante Pääbo, Stephan Riesenberg
pmc-12689631.description: The selection of cells that have acquired a desired gene edit is often done by the introduction of additional genes that confer drug resistance or encode fluorophores. However, such marker genes can have unintended physiological effects and are not compatible with editing of single nucleotides.

pmc-13028163.title: A Dissolving Microneedle Design for Poorly Water-Soluble Drugs for Enhanced Skin Permeation and Transdermal Delivery Fabricated Using 3D Printing
pmc-13028163.creator: Sung Giu Jin
pmc-13028163.description: Microneedles (MNs) offer a transformative platform for transdermal drug delivery, though balancing structural precision with mechanical robustness remains challenging. This study utilized SLA 3D printing to fabricate high-resolution MN masters, systematically evaluating printing angles (0° to 60°) and aspect ratios to optimize fidelity. A 45° printing angle was found to significantly enhance tip sharpness and insertion efficiency.

pmc-13215594.title: Nonlinear kernel-based high-dimensional inference for set-based genetic association studies
pmc-13215594.creator: Zechen Zhang, Hui Yang, Meilin Zhu, Ran Guo, Fuzhao Chen, Hui Dong, Yuehua Cui, Haitao Yang
pmc-13215594.description: Nonlinear genetic architectures, including epistasis and threshold effects, are increasingly recognized as contributors to complex disease risk, yet most existing SNP-set association tests rely on linear modeling assumptions, resulting in reduced power and unstable inference when genetic effects are nonlinear or heterogeneously distributed across variants.

pmc-13448011.title: Comment on “Infection outbreaks caused by Carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales: An epidemiological surveillance study in public hospitals in Chile, 2017–2024”
pmc-13448011.creator: Dilip Kumar Kakru, Hima Bindu Mantravadi, Pankaj Nainwal, Apoorva Makan, Fayaz Ahamed

pmc-13567653.title: Teacher-Identified Priorities and Resource Use in Government-Supported School Food and Nutrition Education in Korea
pmc-13567653.creator: Seung Jae Lee, Jieun Oh, Kyung Won Lee
pmc-13567653.description: Background/Objectives: Government-supported school food and nutrition education depends on whether teachers can locate and use relevant programs and resources. This study identified teachers’ perceived priority topics and examined their awareness, use, and barriers regarding government resources in Korea. Methods: A nationwide voluntary online survey was completed by 1273 elementary, middle, and high school teachers between October and November 2024.

pmc-13578983.title: Dietary supplementation with raw potato starch enhanced tibia mass of meat ducks potentially linked to intestine-derived inflammation
pmc-13578983.creator: Jixue Yin, Xin Yue, Simeng Qin, Yuying Huang, Minh Tu Nguyen, Herinda Pertiwi, Yanqun Huang, Rui Zheng, Wen Chen, Huaiyong Zhang
pmc-13578983.description: Gait problems in poultry is a welfare issue with a prevalence of about 21% in commercial meat ducks, which compromises growth performance by restricting access to feed and water. This study evaluated the effects of raw potato starch (RPS) on intestinal barrier function and bone metabolism in both healthy and enteritis-affected meat ducks.
